verdict.rationale: The only on-topic evidence is a community comment. It says newly indexed documents become searchable after an index refresh, and the refresh interval can be tuned to be 'practically real-time' at some performance cost. It also claims the default refresh is about a minute, which means out-of-the-box visibility is not near real time. Missing for 10: first-party documentation of near-real-time refresh behavior, explicit evidence that updates and deletes become searchable incrementally without a full reindex, and independent hands-on corroboration.
